dedupe_keys.name: leak simulations in an experimental testbed water distribution system texas a m acoustic and pressure signals

description: This benchmark dataset holds 280 sensor recordings of controlled leak experiments in a laboratory water distribution testbed at Texas A&M University, made of 152.4 mm PVC pipes 47 m long, and is described in a Data in Brief article. Each 30 second signal comes from an accelerometer, a hydrophone or a dynamic pressure sensor, for looped and branched topologies, four leak types (orifice, longitudinal crack, circumferential crack, gasket) and a no-leak case, and six background conditions of flow and traffic or tool noise. Coverage is one laboratory testbed. The raw signals are a free download from Mendeley Data under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: a small plastic testbed differs from buried field networks in pipe material, length and noise, so methods trained here need field testing. Simulation uses: developing and comparing acoustic and pressure-transient leak detection and localization methods for water network monitoring. Related records: LeakDB (data-leakdb), BattLeDIM (data-battledim-leakage-detection-benchmark) and the Slovak network anomaly dataset (data-slovak-wdn-scada-anomaly-leak-labels).
